_readme: The NIST CCVS85 conformance ledger. Machine-readable, committed, and the single source of truth for where the work stands. Read it before doing anything; update it after every verified change. It replaces the hand-written HANDOFF-*.md files, which were re-derived from scratch each session and drifted. Protocol: .claude/skills/nist-grind/SKILL.md
goal: Every in-scope module at 100% on BOTH axes: every program compiles under `nist_conformance strict`, and every program runs to completion reporting 0 failures in its own CCVS report.

rules.never_ask_take_the_recommended_action: OPERATOR RULING 2026-08-29, given twice — do NOT stop to ask. When a choice arises, take the recommended course of action and proceed. Record the decision and the reasoning in this ledger so it can be reviewed after the fact, but never block the loop on a question.
rules.ix301m_out_of_scope: OPERATOR RULING 2026-08-29 — IX301M is OUT OF SCOPE. It tests INTERMEDIATE-subset flagging, and every construct it expects flagged (ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED, ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM, RECORD KEY IS, the NOT INVALID KEY phrases) is one PowerRustCOBOL implements. A high-subset implementation must not flag features it supports, so its 7 expectations are unreachable by design rather than by defect. IX is scored out of 41.
rules.start_rl_now: OPERATOR RULING 2026-08-29 — START RELATIVE I/O NOW, before IX is finished. This deliberately suspends GOLDEN RULE #9's one-module-at-a-time ordering: IX106A tests DELETE and REWRITE across relative, sequential and indexed files together, so IX cannot close without an RL engine. RL is the largest single piece of work outstanding.
rules.redb_becomes_the_default: OPERATOR RULING 2026-08-29 — fix duplicate-retrieval ordering in the redb engine, which already keeps a `seq` table for it, AND MAKE REDB THE DEFAULT disk engine. This avoids a PRCIDXD1 format change but is a large change in its own right: every `STORAGE IS DISK` file moves to redb, including the ones NC's and SQ's tests run through. Expect to spend iterations on the gate; revert rather than chase.
rules.everything_is_technical_debt: OPERATOR RULING 2026-08-29 — until all NIST implementation is done, there are NO new features; everything is technical debt being paid. Consequences: all of it goes on the `fixes` branch, none of it splits into a features commit, and none of it belongs on forum f=96. This overrides the usual feature/fix classification for the duration, and it covers RL (Relative I/O) too, which is missing COBOL-85 that should already have worked rather than a capability beyond the standard.
rules.no_forum_posts: OPERATOR RULING 2026-08-29 — do not post to cobolforo.es at all while the grind is running. Announcements are batched and are the operator's call.
rules.commit_and_push_before_stopping: OPERATOR RULING 2026-08-29 — never end a session with work uncommitted. Commit and push `fixes` before stopping, subject only to the São Paulo push window (inside it, commit and defer the push).
rules.one_module_at_a_time: GOLDEN RULE #9 — finish the current module on both axes before starting the next. Record a tempting fix in another module under `parked` and move on.
rules.two_axes_never_conflated: Compile is the strictly weaker claim. Never quote it as if it meant the programs work.
rules.full_regression_after_every_change: Re-run the whole-suite strict census AND the execution pass for every finished module, not just the one in flight. The runtime is shared.
rules.deleted_is_not_passed: `***** ****TEST DELETED****` means the program failed its own setup and skipped the case. Track the DELETED count: it fell 108 -> 1 at 1.62.53 while the clean-program count barely moved, and that was real progress a failures-only reading would have missed.
rules.gate_protects_finished_modules_absolutel: The regression gate is ABSOLUTE for finished modules (NC, SQ) and for the whole-suite compile census: those figures must match exactly or the change is reverted. For the module IN FLIGHT the score may legitimately FALL when a harness-fidelity change makes the measurement more honest — assertions that were unreachable start running and start failing. That happened at 1.62.57: IX went 484 -> 482 PASS because IX103A finally found the file IX102A writes, so its scan ran 35 records deep instead of dying on the first READ, and two assertions that had never executed began to fail truthfully. When this happens, SAY SO explicitly with the reason; never revert a fidelity gain to protect a number, and never let a fidelity loss hide behind one.

out_of_scope.sg_ruling: 2026-08-29, operator: SG (Segmentation) is excluded too. Segmentation exists to fit a program into a machine too small to hold it — SECTION headers carry a segment-number and the runtime overlays the independent segments over one another. RustCOBOL is a 64-bit solution on 64-bit systems with more address space than any COBOL program can exhaust, so a segment-number COMPILES and has no effect at all. There is no behaviour for the module to measure, and scoring it would score a mechanism that will never exist. Its 13 programs still compile; they are reported N-A rather than deleted, so the exclusion stays visible.

RL.name: Relative I/O
RL.finished_at: 1.62.77 — from a 14/35 baseline in one session. Scored out of 34: RL301M is excluded from execution by the same ruling as IX301M (rules.ix301m_out_of_scope) and still counts in the compile census, where it passes.
RL.engine_landed: 1.62.76 — `cobolt-runtime/src/relative.rs`, container PRCREL1, plus MEMORY. All seven verbs dispatch on FileOrganization::Relative. The same version taught the harness RL's ten chained members, which is what ended the four timeouts.
RL.what_actually_closed_it: The engine was the smaller half. Three front-end fixes at 1.62.77 took RL from 24 to 34: (1) `RELATIVE data-name` with the word KEY omitted was read as a bare organization clause and the key silently dropped, so every random WRITE returned 24 — eight programs, one clause; (2) file status 14, a sequential READ whose record number needs more digits than the RELATIVE KEY item holds — the PICTURE's width is part of the file's behaviour; (3) an unterminated conditional phrase (`WRITE ... INVALID KEY GO TO X` with no END-WRITE) read past the enclosing ELSE, so RL210A did not parse at all. The last one is general, not relative-specific, and raised the whole-suite compile census to 423.
RL.operator_ruling: 2026-08-29 — IMPLEMENT Relative file support as the NIST suite expects it, and treat it as TECHNICAL DEBT, not a feature: RELATIVE is COBOL-85 that should already have worked, so under GOLDEN RULE #4 it is a fix. It goes on the `fixes` branch like everything else, needs no features commit, and is not an f=96 item. This is the one place in the queue where building missing capability is authorised; elsewhere a genuine grammar gap is still recorded and parked, not invented.
RL.starting_point: HISTORICAL, superseded by engine_landed above. Before 1.62.76 there was no RELATIVE engine at all: the parser accepted `ORGANIZATION IS RELATIVE` (FileOrganization::Relative) and nothing in the runtime ever matched that variant — no dispatch, no engine, no diagnostic — so a program declaring it compiled cleanly and then misbehaved silently.
scope_notes: A RELATIVE file is addressed by RELATIVE KEY, an integer record number from 1, not by a key embedded in the record.
SELECT carries `RELATIVE KEY IS data-name`; the parser must keep it as RECORD KEY is kept for INDEXED.
All three access modes: SEQUENTIAL (records in relative-number order), RANDOM (by RELATIVE KEY), DYNAMIC (both).
Verbs to dispatch on FileOrganization::Relative: OPEN, CLOSE, READ (random and NEXT/PREVIOUS), WRITE, REWRITE, DELETE, START.
File statuses the module tests: 00, 02, 10, 21, 22, 23, 24 (boundary violation on WRITE past the end), 43, 46, 47, 48, 49.
A deleted slot must stay addressable and read as not-present — a relative file is a numbered slot table, not a dense list.
Reuse the storage split the INDEXED engines already have (STORAGE IS MEMORY | DISK) rather than inventing a fourth container format.
RL.sequencing: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-29 — the operator ruled START RL NOW, before IX is finished (see rules.start_rl_now). IX106A cannot pass without it. It is large enough to be worth planning before coding, but as technical debt it does NOT need the feature pipeline — plan it in the ledger's work_queue and implement on `fixes`.

work_queue.title: WITHDRAWN AND CORRECTED — `extract` is not what the harness runs, and diagnosing from it invents defects
work_queue.the_mistake: At 1.62.93 this entry claimed IC201A's three failures were a harness gap because its callee was never concatenated. THAT WAS WRONG, and it was wrong in a way worth keeping: `extract IC201A` yields one program, running that by hand produced eleven `CALL to unknown program 'IC202A'` warnings, and the conclusion followed. But the harness does NOT run what `extract` emits — `with_subprograms` (nist_conformance.rs ~1535) appends every member whose `subprogram_of` names the caller, and only the RUN path uses it.
work_queue.how_it_was_caught: Arithmetic, not luck. `run IC` scores IC201A at 3 FAIL / 9 PASS. If IC202A were genuinely absent, all eleven calls would take the ON OVERFLOW branch and far more than three assertions would fail. The same check kills it elsewhere: IC103A's CALL-TEST-06 `.01` PASSES, and it can only pass if IC104A actually wrote `IC104` into the caller's field.
work_queue.the_lesson: When running a member by hand to diagnose it, RECONSTRUCT WHAT THE HARNESS RUNS — the member plus its `subprogram_of` members concatenated — or the diagnosis is against a different program from the one being scored. `extract` is a convenience for reading source, not a faithful reproduction of a run. Everything the earlier iteration concluded about IC201A stands withdrawn; its three ON OVERFLOW failures are still unexplained and are NOT a missing callee.
work_queue.still_worth_doing: The sweep the withdrawn entry proposed is still a good idea, but for the opposite reason: run each member THE WAY THE HARNESS DOES and look for `CALL to unknown program`, to find any caller whose callee genuinely is not declared. Header counts off `extract` cannot answer that question — IC103A, IC106A and IC201A all show one header and all of them do get their callees at run time.
work_queue.faithful_repro_recipe: VERIFIED at 1.62.93. `extract IC201A` and `extract IC202A` into a scratch directory OUTSIDE the repo, concatenate them in that order, and run the result: `rcrun run IC201A-unit.cbl --source-format fixed --switch XXXXX051=ON --switch XXXXX052=OFF`. That reproduces `with_subprograms` exactly — ZERO `CALL to unknown program` warnings, and IC201A's same three failures. Use this shape for any IC member with a callee; it is the difference between debugging the scored program and debugging a different one.
work_queue.the_open_puzzle_for_IC201A: With the callee present and no unresolved call, the report STILL carries `OVERFLOW SHOULD NOT OCCUR` — and that string is written ONLY inside the overflow phrases of CALL-TEST-03. CALL-TEST-03 scores 1 PASS / 3 FAIL over four assertions and exercises THREE forms of the statement: `CALL "lit" … ON OVERFLOW` (03-01), `CALL "lit" … OVERFLOW` with the optional ON omitted (03-02), and `CALL ID1 …` with an identifier target, `ID1 PIC X(6) VALUE "IC202A"` (03-03).
work_queue.RULED_OUT_at_1_62_93: The CALL/OVERFLOW machinery itself is CORRECT in all three forms. A direct repro (`ovf.cbl` in the scratch dir) calls a program that exists, three times, once per form, each with an overflow phrase that would stamp a marker — and all three leave the marker untouched. So the phrase does not fire on a successful call, the bare `OVERFLOW` spelling parses (`is_word(p.peek(), "OVERFLOW")`, stmt.rs ~3177), and an identifier target resolves. None of those is the defect, and none of them should be investigated again.
work_queue.what_is_left: Something writes `OVERFLOW SHOULD NOT OCCUR` into RE-MARK when the phrase provably did not run, OR RE-MARK survives from an assertion that did write it into one that did not. Note all four assertions report as sub-test `.03`, so REC-CT is not advancing across 03-01/02/03 either — one explanation could cover both. The next step is to instrument the member itself: insert DISPLAYs of RE-MARK and REC-CT at the head of CALL-TEST-03-01, -02 and -03 in a scratch copy of the faithful run unit, and see which paragraph actually reaches which. Do NOT theorise further from reading; two readings have now been wrong here.
work_queue.caveat: Do NOT widen the SUBRTN rule by guessing. Treating SUBPRG as a callee at 1.62.82 broke SQ (85/85 -> 84/84) and was reverted inside the same change; the two cards mean different things and the difference is load-bearing.

work_queue.title: A REDEFINES inside ANY nested program is never established — the two descriptions do not share storage
work_queue.worth: IC106A's 3 failures, and it REACHES PAST THE SUITE: every RAD form event handler is a nested program, so a developer writing REDEFINES in a handler's WORKING-STORAGE gets two independent slots and silently wrong data. That makes this a product defect that NIST happened to find, not a conformance detail.
work_queue.PROVEN_at_1_62_92: Two repros in `crates/cobolt-runtime/tests/test_linkage_redefines.rs`, both `#[ignore]`d as known defects so the suite stays green — run them with `--ignored`. The first is IC106A's shape (a callee writes through a LINKAGE REDEFINES of its parameter, the caller reads the parameter). The SECOND has no LINKAGE and no parameter at all: a nested program redefines its OWN WORKING-STORAGE, writes the parts, reads the whole. Both fail, which is what proves the cause is not about parameter binding.
work_queue.the_real_cause: `push_local_scope` (environment.rs ~2734) inserts a nested program's items into `store` and `symbols` and does NOTHING ELSE. The redefinition machinery — the equivalence classes, the `redefine_aliases` for over-budget layout-identical members, and the refresh that keeps small classes in step — is all built when the environment is constructed from the OUTER program's DATA DIVISION. A nested program's items arrive later, by a path that never builds any of it, so its redefining item is simply an independent slot.
work_queue.supersedes: The 1.62.91 entry `a-redefines-in-linkage-is-never-bound`, which blamed `layout_keys` excluding REDEFINES from the CALL pairing. That exclusion is real and correct for its own purpose, but it is NOT this defect: the second repro has no pairing involved and fails identically.
work_queue.evidence: Measured at 1.62.91. All three read BLANK where X, Y and Z are expected — `COMPUTED=` is empty, not wrong. IC106A's own comment says what it is checking: 'THIS TEST VERIFIES THAT DATA WAS MOVED TO A REDEFINED ITEM IN THE LINKAGE SECTION OF IC107.' The caller then reads `DN2 (8)`, `DN2 (9)`, `DN2 (10)`. Empty rather than stale means the storage was never bound at all.
work_queue.cause: `layout_keys` is built with `.filter(|(_, c)| c.level != 88 && c.level != 66 && c.redefines.is_none())` (environment.rs ~1161). Excluding REDEFINES is CORRECT for its original purpose — a redefinition is a second description of storage its target already owns, and counting it made a group twice as wide (the comment there says so). But the CALL path reuses `layout_keys` as the list of things to bind, and a redefinition of a bound parameter is exactly something that must resolve to the caller's storage.
work_queue.fix_sketch: Establish a nested program's redefinitions when its scope is pushed, the way the outer program's are established when the environment is built. The machinery already exists and is not duplicated — the work is calling it with the nested program's declarations and unwinding it in `pop_local_scope`. Size the two paths separately: the small-class REFRESH keeps descriptions in step by copying on write, and the over-budget path installs `redefine_aliases`; a nested program needs whichever its own class falls into, by the same budget rule.
work_queue.acceptance: Remove the two `#[ignore]` attributes in `test_linkage_redefines.rs`. They are written as the criterion and both must pass. Then re-measure IC106A, which should lose its 3 failures.
work_queue.caveat: `pop_local_scope` must undo whatever is installed, or a redefinition from one call leaks into the next program — the same discipline the parameter aliases already follow with `aliased` / `alias_target`. A leak here would be worse than the defect, because it would corrupt an UNRELATED program's storage.

work_queue.title: A group parameter's subordinates are paired BY POSITION, but LINKAGE is a view over the caller's BYTES
work_queue.worth: 9 failures — IC235A 5 and IC103A 4, the module's largest remaining bucket, and the suite says outright they are the same shape.
work_queue.diagnosis: DECISIVE, from reading IC103A and IC104A side by side. IC103A's own section header states the case: 'THE ITEM DESCRIPTIONS ARE DIFFERENT IN THE SUBPROGRAM FROM THE MAIN PROGRAM, BUT THE NUMBER OF CHARACTERS IS IDENTICAL.' IC104A's header says the same from its side. The two programs describe the SAME BYTES with a DIFFERENT TREE.
work_queue.the_data: GROUP-01 (10 chars) in the caller is `02 ALPHA-NUM-FIELD X(5)` then `02 GROUP-LEV2` containing `03 NUMER-FIELD 99` and `03 ALPHA-FIELD A(3)` — two top-level children. GRP-01 in the callee is `02 AN-FIELD X(5)`, `02 NUM-DISPLAY 99`, `02 GRP-LEVEL` containing `03 A-FIELD A(3)` — THREE top-level children. By byte offset the leaves align exactly: (0,5), (5,2), (7,3). By tree position they do not. GROUP-02 (8 chars) is the mirror: caller has `02 NUM-ITEM S99` + `02 ALPHA-EDITED X(6)`, callee has one `02 GRP-03` holding both.
work_queue.why_the_pass_fail_split_proves_it: CALL-TEST-06 .01 passes (ALPHA-NUM-FIELD/AN-FIELD, both the FIRST child, so position and offset agree) and .04 passes (ELEM-77/ELEM-01, an elementary 77-level passed directly, no tree at all). .02, .03, .05 and .06 fail — every one of them a subordinate whose POSITION differs from its OFFSET. Nothing else in the module has that signature.
work_queue.where: The positional pairing landed at 1.62.85 ('a group parameter's subordinate items are paired with the argument's BY POSITION and aliased in lock-step'). That was a real improvement over by-name — it freed the two programs from having to agree on names — but position is the wrong axis. COBOL-85 gives LINKAGE a view over the caller's storage: the callee's description lays ITS OWN items over the caller's bytes, and neither the names nor the shape of the tree has to match.
options: BY OFFSET (smaller): for each LEAF of the callee's parameter compute (offset, length) within the group, find the caller's leaf covering exactly those bytes, and alias to it. Closes IC103A and IC235A — every leaf aligns in both. Fails when the two descriptions split the same bytes differently (`PIC X(4)` against two `PIC XX`), which the standard permits and this pair does not exercise.

SHARED BUFFER (correct): the group parameter is one byte buffer both programs view through their own descriptions, the way `RecordLayout::materialize`/`distribute` already does for an FD record. Handles every case including unaligned splits. Larger: it changes how a group parameter is stored, not just how it is bound.

Do the offset mapping now and record the unaligned case as a known deviation. It is a strict improvement over position, it is measurable against the suite today, and the buffer model can replace it later without the callers changing.
work_queue.recommendation: Take the third. The offset mapping is the smaller half of the correct answer and is not thrown away by it — `files.rs` already owns the buffer machinery if the full model is wanted later, so this does not paint into a corner. Measure IC235A separately after landing it: it is 5 failures and only ASSUMED to be the same shape.
work_queue.attempted_1_62_90: The offset mapping WAS tried and reverted — see the `pairing-linkage-leaves-by-byte-offset` dead end. It moved IC103A 4 -> 3 and IC235A 5 -> 4, so the direction is right, and it took IC203A from 1 -> 7, so the mapping is not. Read that entry before trying again: the two suspects are `item_width`'s `unwrap_or(0)` silently zeroing a leaf it cannot render (which shifts every offset after it) and the per-occurrence expansion of an OCCURS item. VERIFY THE OFFSETS BEFORE TRUSTING THEM — dump `leaf_layout` for both sides and check the widths sum to the group width.
work_queue.next_probe: Read `files.rs` `compute_layout` first — it already walks a record description into (offset, len) per item and is the obvious thing to reuse rather than write a second offset walker in `environment.rs`. That advice stands and was NOT followed at 1.62.90: a second walker was written against `item_width` instead, and `item_width` is where the suspicion now falls.

work_queue.resolved_at: 1.62.89 — IC227A 11 failures -> 1, and 8 of its 23 tests executing successfully -> 18. IC 212 -> 222 PASS / 44 -> 34 FAIL, 82.8% -> 86.7%. It was TWO defects stacked, and the second was invisible until the first was fixed: (1) `NestedProgram` now carries its own FILE STATUS bindings, swapped in around the call, with a miss falling back to `file_specs` for the GLOBAL-file case; (2) `set_file_status` resolved the name through `resolve_name` instead of writing a raw key — a status item can be a LINKAGE item, and `set_str` keys by `storage_key`, which follows REDEFINES but NOT the parameter aliases. Fixing only (1) moved the five `.02` assertions and left all five `.01`s exactly as they were.
work_queue.title: RESOLVED — A file's FILE STATUS item is resolved from the OUTER program, so a subprogram reports into the caller's storage
work_queue.worth: 10 of IC227A's 11 failures — the module's largest bucket, and one cause. Every failure is the same swapped pair.
work_queue.diagnosis: DECISIVE, from running IC227A by hand and reading both SELECTs. The two programs share an EXTERNAL file and each names its OWN status item: IC227A has `FILE STATUS IS EXTERNAL-FILE-FS` in WORKING-STORAGE, IC227A-1 has `FILE STATUS IS LINKAGE-FS` in its LINKAGE SECTION (the caller's third argument, `F-S-PARAM`). The FILE is shared, which is right; the STATUS ITEM is a property of each program's own SELECT and is not.

work_queue.title: RESOLVED — A REWRITE that CHANGES an alternate key must join the end of its new duplicate set
work_queue.worth: IX215A's last 2 failures, and very likely IX211A's 2 as well — its symptoms are small ordering errors in a walk over duplicate keys.
work_queue.diagnosis: DECISIVE, from the data rather than a repro. IX215A GF-08 reads record 176 and rewrites it with ALTKEY2 = 'DCDCDCDCDC100ALTKEY2'. GF-09 then reads record **4** and rewrites it with the SAME value, deliberately creating a duplicate set of two, and STARTs on the 2-character generic key 'DC' expecting record **176** — the entry created FIRST. A dump of the file confirms exactly two records carry that value, 4 and 176. We return 4.
work_queue.the_rule: Duplicates are retrieved in the order their entries entered the set. Record 176 joined in GF-08, record 4 in GF-09, so 176 comes first. We order by the record's ORIGINAL insertion sequence — record 4 was written before 176 when the file was built — which is a position record 4 never held in this set. CLAUDE.md's note that 'the record keeps its original insertion sequence across a REWRITE' is right only while the alternate VALUE is unchanged; when the value changes the record leaves one duplicate set and joins another, at the end.
work_queue.where: Disk engine (the default): `alt_tree_key(ks, rec, recid)` appends the RecordId, so ordering within one alternate value is by RecordId — permanently the original write order. Fixing it means the tiebreaker must be a per-entry sequence assigned when the entry is inserted, not the RecordId. That is a container-format consideration for PRCIDXD1, so size it before starting. The redb engine already keeps a `seq` table for this and may only need its sequence reassigned on a value-changing REWRITE; the in-memory engine uses a BTreeSet of primary keys and has the same original-order problem.
work_queue.caveat: Only a REWRITE that CHANGES the alternate value reassigns the sequence. One that leaves it alone must keep its position, which is what the existing behaviour and the disk-parity note are about.
work_queue.sizing_2026_08_29: Measured, not estimated. The disk engine builds an alternate entry key as `altvalue || recid.to_be_bytes()` (alt_tree_key, ~line 820) and `index_remove` rebuilds that same key from the OLD record plus the recid — which works only because the suffix is derivable from the record. A sequence suffix is not derivable, so removal and value-changing rewrite would need a persisted per-alternate `recid -> seq` map. The container header carries a version field (currently 1u16 at offset 8), so a bump is possible, but this is a PRCIDXD1 FORMAT CHANGE to the DEFAULT on-disk engine — the same engine NC's and SQ's file tests run through. Cost: format version 2, a new persisted structure, changes to index_insert / index_remove / rewrite, the key_prefix klen logic, and a read path for version-1 files. Benefit: 4 assertions in 2 programs (IX215A, IX211A).
alternatives: Do the format change. Correct, and the only route to 42/42 on this axis, but the most expensive remaining item and the one with real risk to the protected modules.
Do it in the redb engine only, which already keeps a `seq` table for exactly this — cheap there, but redb is not the default, so the suite would not see it without switching the default.
Accept it as a known deviation and record it. Duplicate retrieval order after a value-changing REWRITE is a narrow corner; the cost/benefit is poor at 4 assertions.
work_queue.operator_call: This one is a judgement call about cost, not a diagnosis gap. Do not start the format change without a decision.

dead_ends.what: Carry a nested program's REDEFINES overlays on `NestedProgram` — `redefine_state()` off the environment its DATA DIVISION is already analysed into — then `adopt_redefine_state` on the shared env at `push_local_scope` and `drop_redefine_state` at pop, removing only what that call newly introduced.

dead_ends.and_this_is_the_part_worth_reading: BOTH acceptance tests PASSED. `a_nested_programs_own_redefines_shares_its_storage` and `a_callee_writing_through_a_linkage_redefines_reaches_the_caller` were written as the criterion, the fix satisfied both, and the module still got worse. The redefinition genuinely started working and something ELSE broke because of it. The tests are necessary and NOT sufficient, and their `#[ignore]` text now says so.
dead_ends.the_likely_mechanism: Every CCVS member carries a boilerplate report area full of redefinitions — `COMPUTED-N REDEFINES COMPUTED-A`, `COMPUTED-0V18`, `COMPUTED-4V14`, `CM-18V0`, `CORRECT-N` and more, all over the same twenty bytes. Those live in the nested programs too. Inert, they were harmless; live, every write to one refreshes the others across a shared area, and the small-class REFRESH path re-renders one description and distributes it across another on EVERY write anywhere inside either. That is the CCVS report's own formatting fields, so a member can start mis-printing its results without any test logic changing.
dead_ends.what_to_do_instead: Do not adopt a nested program's overlays wholesale. Two directions, neither tried: (1) adopt only the overlays that involve a BOUND PARAMETER, leaving a nested program's private redefinitions alone — that is enough for IC106A's LINK-TEST-06, which is about a redefinition of LINKAGE, and touches none of the report boilerplate; (2) find out first whether the report regression is the refresh path or the alias path by adopting one and not the other, since they have different costs and different failure modes. Measure IC106A's report text directly, not just its score — if the failures changed shape rather than merely growing, the boilerplate theory is confirmed.

dead_ends.the_diagnosis_is_still_right: Do not discard the analysis in `group-parameter-is-a-view-over-bytes-not-a-tree-of-names`. The two members' own headers say the descriptions differ in shape and agree in size, the offsets line up and the tree positions do not, and the pass/fail split (.01 and .04 pass, .02/.03/.05/.06 fail) matches that and nothing else. Position IS the wrong axis. The MAPPING built on top of it is what was wrong.
dead_ends.where_to_look_first: NARROWED at 1.62.90, but NOT closed — read this before re-attempting. The member's own failing assertion is `CNCL-TEST-05 ... TABLE-2 INCORRECT`, and `TABLE-2` is the interesting shape: IC203A declares it `02 DN6 PICTURE X OCCURS 2 TIMES` (ONE child, twice) and IC205A declares the same two bytes as `02 TV-1 PIC X` + `02 TV-2 PIC X` (TWO children). Positional pairing zips [DN6] against [TV-1, TV-2] and binds only TV-1 — half the group — and IC203A still scored 1 failure. The offset attempt scored 7, so it must have bound FEWER than that, not more.
dead_ends.occurs_suspicion_weakened: `occurrence_keys` (environment.rs ~1750) DOES expand dimensions: for each `layout_key` it pushes one `subscript_key` per occurrence, honouring ODO. So the walk should have produced `DN6(1)@0 len 1` and `DN6(2)@1 len 1`, which match TV-1 and TV-2 exactly. Suspect (2) as originally written is therefore probably wrong, and the fact that this SHOULD have worked is itself the clue.
dead_ends.suspects_1_and_2_are_RULED_OUT: MEASURED at 1.62.91 by `crates/cobolt-runtime/tests/test_linkage_layout_probe.rs`, which is kept. Every storage property an offset walk depends on holds for exactly IC203A's shape: the two descriptions of TABLE-2 agree at 2 bytes; NO leaf reports width 0, including the unsubscripted `DN6` (so `item_width`'s `unwrap_or(0)` is not firing here); `DN6(1)` and `DN6(2)` are addressable and hold their own byte; and writing an occurrence SURFACES IN THE GROUP, which is the direction a callee writes in. The offset walk would therefore have computed the right layout and an alias onto an occurrence is observable from the caller. Neither of the first two suspects survives.
dead_ends.remaining_suspect: The alias LIFECYCLE in the CALL path, not the layout. What is left is how the aliases are established and released around the call — `aliased` / `alias_target` restore, `restore_after` for BY CONTENT, `push_local_scope`, and the static-locals snapshot in `program_locals`. IC203A's subject is CANCEL in a subprogram and its failing assertion is a CANCEL test, so the interaction between a WIDER set of aliases and the CANCEL lifecycle is the live hypothesis. Note the attempt aliased strictly more items than positional pairing did; the regression is therefore something going wrong *because* more was bound, not less.
dead_ends.what_to_do_instead: The layout is not the problem — stop investigating it. Instrument the CALL path instead: for IC203A's `CALL "IC205A" USING TABLE-1, TABLE-2, DN1`, log the pairs actually aliased, then what is released on return, then what CANCEL does to them. Compare a run under positional pairing with one under offset pairing; the two differ only in the extra pairs, so whichever of those is still bound (or still redirected) after the call is the defect. Do NOT re-attempt the pairing blind a second time.

dead_ends.what: Make `push_local_scope` SHADOW a name the caller already has instead of skipping it, so a called program's data is its own.
dead_ends.why_it_failed: IC 10 -> 5 of 25, 187 -> 138 PASS, and one member began timing out. Binding is by-name copy-in/copy-out: only the names in `PROCEDURE DIVISION USING` are copied in. Shadowing gives the callee fresh slots for EVERY name it declares — including the subordinate items of a group parameter — and those are not copied in, so a callee that reads `GRP-01`'s children saw their initial values instead of the caller's data. The old aliasing-by-collision was accidentally right for exactly that case.
dead_ends.the_defect_is_still_real: IC201A CALL-TEST-02 does `CALL "IC202A" USING DN1, DN2, DN1, DN4` — the third argument is DN1, not DN3. IC202A writes through its third LINKAGE item, which it happens to call `DN3`, and the caller's own unrelated `DN3` is overwritten because the two are the same slot. The test checks precisely that: `DN3 VALUE CHANGED BY CALL`.
dead_ends.what_to_do_instead: Alias, do not copy. Bind the callee's parameter name — and everything subordinate to it — to the CALLER's storage for the length of the call, the way `addr_aliases` already redirects `resolve_name` for pointers. Then a group parameter's children resolve through the alias to the caller's children, a name the callee declares that is NOT a parameter gets a private slot, and BY CONTENT is a copy made once at entry with no write-back. Size the subordinate-item part first: that is where this attempt broke.

dead_ends.what: Keep a separator COMMA OR SEMICOLON when the next token is a sign, so `FUNCTION MOD(A, -3)` stops reading as one subtraction.
dead_ends.why_it_failed: It fixed IF but broke NC245A, which had been passing — NC 95/95 -> 94/95, a protected baseline. NC245A is the separator test itself and writes `MOVE ELEM3( +3; +5, +10) TO TEMP`: a semicolon is never a list separator in COBOL, only decoration, and no parser eats one, so keeping it is a parse error rather than a separator.
dead_ends.what_to_do_instead: The exception belongs to the COMMA alone. Both the function-argument and subscript parsers already eat a comma between elements, so keeping it there costs nothing; the semicolon has no such reader anywhere.
dead_ends.the_lesson: The regression was invisible in the module being worked on and only showed up in the whole-suite gate. Run every finished module after ANY lexer or parser change — those two crates have no module boundary.

protected_baselines._when: Operator ruling, 2026-08-29: checked once per MODULE, not once per change. Running every finished module after every fix caught four problems across the whole grind, which does not pay for re-measuring 7000+ assertions each time.
